newsitem.title: USA: Mortgage rates fell this week.
newsitem.headline: Mortgage rates fell this week.

text.p: Average interest rates on 30-year and 15-year fixed-rate mortgages fell in the week ending Nov. 1 from the previous week, the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp. said Thursday.
Freddie Mac said rates on 30-year mortgages averaged 7.78 percent, down eight basis points from 7.86 percent last week.
Fifteen-year loans fell to an average 7.30 percent from 7.37 percent the previous week.
But adjustable rate mortgages inched upward to an average 5.60 percent from 5.57 percent last week, it said.
A year ago, rates on 30-year loans averaged 7.44 percent, for 15-year mortgages they were at 6.97 percent, and ARM rates were at 5.67 percent.
Frank Nothaft, deputy chief economist for Freddie Mac, said recent reports on declines in U.S. home sales were "consistent with the slowdown of the economy.
"Consequently, news of the slower growth encouraged long-term interest rates to move downward this week," Nothaft said.
Last Friday the National Association of Realtors reported a 2.9 percent decrease in sales of existing homes in September to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 4.02 million units.
On Wednesday the Commerce Department said new home sales fell 0.5 percent last month to an annual rate of 816,000 units.
The Labour Department will issue October employment data Friday morning.

Freddie Mac said lenders charged an average 1.8 percent in fees and points on 30-year loans and 1.5 percent on ARM loans, both unchanged from last week. They charged 1.7 percent on 15-year mortgages, down from 1.8 percent last week.
